question: Can a 14B model reach reasoning performance of much larger models by centring the training recipe on synthetic data quality, a tuned data mixture and a new DPO pair-generation method?
hypothesis: Data quality, with synthetic data throughout training, can rival gains from scaling compute, and can take a student past its GPT-4o teacher on STEM QA.
contributions: Synthetic data for pretraining and midtraining
Curation and filtering of high-quality organic data
Post-training with refined SFT data and Pivotal Token Search to create DPO pairs

method.summary: A 14B decoder-only transformer (phi-3-medium architecture with tiktoken and full 4K attention) is pretrained on about 10T tokens of a mixture dominated by synthetic data, extended to 16K in midtraining, then post-trained with one SFT round, one DPO round on pivotal-token pairs and one judge-guided DPO round.
method.task: language model pretraining and post-training (SFT, DPO)

datasets.name: Synthetic pretraining data (50 types)
datasets.size: about 400B unweighted tokens; ~290B unique tokens in mixture
datasets.source: GPT-4-family generated from curated seeds; multi-agent prompting, self-revision, instruction reversal
datasets.preprocessing: validated by execution loops and tests for code; plurality-vote answers for questions

datasets.name: Web
datasets.source: filtered web dumps using small classifiers trained on ~10^6 LLM annotations
datasets.preprocessing: n-gram and compression-ratio outlier removal; custom HTML-to-text extractor

datasets.name: Web rewrites
datasets.source: synthetic rewrites of filtered web content

datasets.name: Code data
datasets.source: mixture of synthetic and raw code

datasets.name: Acquired sources
datasets.source: academic data, books, forums (arXiv, PubMed Central, GitHub, licensed books)

datasets.name: SFT data
datasets.source: public prompts plus synthetic; multiple responses, best chosen by LLM evaluation; multilingual data for 40 languages

datasets.name: Pivotal Token DPO data (Table 7)
datasets.size: 3,000 unknown+safety; 132,859 generic multiple-choice Q&A; 76,552 math; 16,080 python; 21,806 cpp/go/java/js/rust
datasets.source: Pivotal Token Search on prompts with ground truth

datasets.name: Judge-guided DPO data (Table 8)
datasets.size: about 850k pairs: 43,842 unknown+safety; 266,000 any vs any overall; 532,000 any vs any accuracy
datasets.source: responses from GPT-4o, GPT-4t and phi-4, labelled by GPT-4o judge

models.name: phi-4
models.architecture: decoder-only transformer, full attention over 4K context (phi-3-medium used a 2K sliding window)

other.note: trained solely on synthetic data, ablation only, over 20 repetitions of each source

other.also: judge for judge-guided DPO and RAI evals; answer extractor for AMC

training.objective: next-token pretraining; SFT; DPO (Rafailov et al. 2023) in two rounds
training.lr: pretraining peak 0.0003; midtraining peak 10x lower; SFT 10^-6

other.midtraining_mix: 30% newly curated longer-context data, 70% recall tokens from pretraining
other.dpo_hyperparameters: not stated (beta, lr, epochs, batch size)
other.pts_samples_per_estimate: not stated for training; N = 529 in Fig 3 illustration
other.dpo_hallucination_data: refusal DPO data used the first 5 tokens of the response
other.data_mixture_search: ablations at 1T-token horizon, 7B scale, transferred to 14B

inference.samples: AMC: 10 independent generations per question per model (Appendix C); Fig 1 caption says 100 runs; HELMET: average across 5 runs
inference.prompting: pretraining evals: log-likelihood for MMLU (5-shot), MMLU-pro, ARCC (1-shot); few-shot 1, 3, 4, 8 for TriviaQA, MBPP, MATH, GSM8k. Post-training evals: simple-evals prompts, extraction and temperature 0.5

metrics.name: simple-evals scores (MMLU, GPQA diamond, MATH, HumanEval, MGSM, SimpleQA F1, DROP)
AMC score
metrics.definition: 6 points correct, 1.5 unanswered, 0 incorrect; max 150 per test; averaged over four tests

metrics.name: RAI defect rate DR-x
metrics.definition: percentage of samples with severity >= x on a 0-7 scale, GPT-4o simulated conversations

eval.protocol: Decontamination by 13-gram and 7-gram hybrid algorithm against 20 benchmarks. AMC tests run after hyperparameters were fixed; three candidate models were scored and the final was chosen on other factors (footnote 8). GPT-4o extracts final answers at temperature 1. Single-run post-training table; no seeds or significance tests.

prompts.text: The following question is from a 25-question, multiple choice test. Each question is followed by answers marked A, B, C, D, and E. Only one of these is correct. SCORING: You will receive 6 points for each correct answer, 1.5 points for each problem left unanswered, and 0 points for each incorrect answer. Solve the question step by step, then answer \boxed{A}, \boxed{B}, \boxed{C}, \boxed{D}, \boxed{E}, or \boxed{blank}.

evidence.quote: The model was pretrained for approximately 10T tokens using linear warm-up and decay schedules with peak learning rate of 0.0003, constant weight decay of 0.1, and global batch size of 5760.

results.claim: phi-4 scores 56.1 on GPQA, above GPT-4o at 50.6.
phi-4 scores 80.4 on MATH, above GPT-4o at 74.6.
results.note: Footnote: Llama-3.3 scores 66.3 here under simple-evals strict formatting, Meta reports 77.

results.claim: Pivotal-token DPO raises GPQA from 47.3 (SFT) to 53.6.
results.setup: simple-evals, phi-4 SFT checkpoint then DPO stage 1 (pivotal token)
results.table: Table 9, row GPQA, column DPO stage 1

results.claim: Pivotal-token DPO raises MATH from 77.1 (SFT) to 80.5.
results.table: Table 9, row MATH, column DPO stage 1

results.claim: Judge-guided DPO alone (stage 2 only) takes ArenaHard from 56.7 to 69.8; with both stages 75.4.
results.setup: SFT checkpoint, DPO stage 2 only; ArenaHard uses a GPT-4 judge
results.table: Table 9, row ArenaHard, column DPO stage 2 only (phi-4 stage 1 + 2 is 75.4)

results.claim: Stage 2 only is worse than stage 1 on MATH (77.6 vs 80.5) and GPQA (52.4 vs 53.6); the authors find the two stages complementary.
results.setup: SFT checkpoint, DPO stage 2 only vs stage 1
results.quote: In general, we find that pivotal token DPO is most useful on reasoning-heavy tasks (GPQA, MATH) while judge-guided DPO is particularly useful for the benchmark that itself involves a GPT-4 judge: ArenaHard.

results.claim: On fresh November 2024 AMC 10/12 tests, phi-4 averages 91.8 out of 150.
results.setup: Four tests, temperature 0.5, max 150; Fig 1 bar values read from figure text (phi-4 91.8, next 89.8 in order printed)
results.quote: This is the average score (with maximum score 150) over the four tests on 100 runs with temperature t = 0.5.

Footnote 8: three candidate models all exceeded 89 and the final was chosen after seeing the other two scores. The baseline 81.6 is read from the figure's value ordering, not labelled per model in the text.

results.claim: phi-4 outperforms Qwen-2.5-14B-Instruct on 9 of 12 benchmarks; weakest on SimpleQA, DROP, IFEval.
results.setup: Table 1 benchmarks incl. internal framework ones
results.quote: phi-4 outperforms the closest in-class contemporary model, Qwen-2.5-14B-Instruct, in 9 out of 12 benchmarks.

results.claim: IFEval is a real weakness: phi-4 scores 63.0 vs Qwen 2.5 14B instruct at 78.7.
results.quote: However, IFEval reveals a real weakness of our model – it has trouble strictly following instructions.

results.claim: Post-training moved SimpleQA outcomes from 90.0% incorrect/6.8% correct (base-stage bar) towards refusals: final 81.1% not attempted, 15.8% incorrect, 3.0% correct.
results.setup: Fig 6 values read from figure; base model vs final phi-4; simple-evals F1 is 3.0 for phi-4 and 7.6 for phi-3
results.note: Bar breakdown read from Fig 6 text layout, ordering of stacks inferred.

results.claim: Synthetic data repeated for 12 epochs beats supplying more fresh web tokens in phase 2 runs.
results.setup: Fig 2, 5-shot MMLU, smaller scale phase 2 pretraining runs, 4 vs 12 epochs
results.quote: We see that despite many epochs on synthetic data, we do not see overfitting behavior and in fact the 12 epoch models perform better than those that have seen more unique web tokens.

results.claim: A 13B model trained only on synthetic data lags phi-3-medium by 14.8 points on TriviaQA.
phi-4 pretrained gains +10.3 on MMLU-pro and +8.9 on MATH over phi-3-medium (4k).
results.table: Table 2, row phi-4 (4k), column MMLU pro

results.claim: Final pretraining mixture: web 15%, web rewrites 15%, synthetic 40%, code 20%, acquired 10%.
results.quote: The remaining tokens are largely sourced from synthetic data which accounts for 40% of the data mixture tokens.

results.claim: Pivotal tokens are chosen by recursive binary search on change in estimated success probability, with prompts filtered to 0.2 <= p(success) <= 0.8.
results.setup: Section 4.3; oracle is test suite for code, ground-truth match for math
results.quote: To improve sample efficiency, we filter the target questions to only include those with 0.2 ≤p(success) ≤0.8, as pivotal tokens are rare for tasks that are very easy or hard.

results.claim: Reference-free long-context: phi-4 at 16K scores 99.0 recall, 36.0 QA on HELMET.
phi-4 jailbreak defect rate 0.073 is the lowest of the models compared; harmful content continuation 0.036 is higher than phi-3 variants.
results.setup: in-house RAI benchmark, GPT-4o simulated conversations; baseline is phi-3 14B-4K

limits: Authors concede factual hallucination (for example invented biographies for 'Who is X?') and weak strict instruction following, especially formatting constraints.
Verbose chain-of-thought answers on simple problems; tuned for single-turn queries.
Contamination: n-gram decontamination is not effective against rephrasing, leaving uncertainty about generalization.
AMC evaluation: final model was picked after seeing the other candidates' AMC scores (footnote 8); Fig 1 caption (100 runs) conflicts with Appendix C (10 generations).
Post-training results come from single runs with no seeds or variance; DPO hyperparameters, PTS thresholds and compute are not given; weights, code and data not released in this report.
SimpleQA is worse by F1 than the base model because post-training trades guesses for refusals.

terms.definition: a token with an outsized effect on the course of the solution, where the probability of a correct answer changes sharply once it is produced

recursively splits a response and estimates p(success) by sampling completions checked with an oracle, keeping single tokens whose probability change exceeds p_gap, then builds DPO pairs from a single accepted and a single rejected token
second DPO round on full-length preference pairs labelled by GPT-4o on accuracy, style and detail

automated process supervision; PTS seen as token-level analogue

code.snippet: if |T|<=1 or |p(success|Tprefix) - p(success|Tprefix+T)| < pgap then return [T]; Tleft,Tright <- Split(T) at the cumulative midpoint of token log probabilities; return Subdivide(Tprefix,Tleft) U Subdivide(Tprefix+Tleft,Tright)
